steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Linear structure: events unfold chronologically — easy to follow, naturalistic tradition. | Key Fact: Non-linear structure: fragmented timeline — creates mystery, reflects psychological states, modernist technique. | Key Fact: Cyclical structure: ends where it began — suggests inevitability, futility, or the impossibility of change. | Key Fact: Tragedy: protagonist with fatal flaw (hamartia) leading to downfall (catharsis for audience).

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Explain the difference between linear and non-linear dramatic structure, giving an example of each. | How does a cyclical structure affect the audience's understanding of a play's themes? | Compare tragedy and comedy as dramatic genres. How do they use different techniques to engage the audience?
